**Open it: [http://maker:4001](http://maker:4001)** (the "Progressive Disclosure" sample already carries a note, so you can see how a note looks)

Every entry now has an **✏ Edit** action. Please try:

1. On any link, click **✏ Edit**. An inline form opens with three fields: **Title**, **Description**, and **Your note**.
2. Correct the title or description if you like, and type something into **Your note** — e.g. *"Use this for the dashboard layout."*
3. Click **Save changes**. The entry updates in place, and your note appears as a **distinct highlighted block labelled "Your note,"** set apart from the page's own fetched description.
4. Try **✏ Edit** again on another link, change something, then press **Cancel** — nothing is kept.

A few choices I made, for your judgment:

- **What's editable:** the title, the description, and a personal note. Are those the right things to correct after saving — or is there something else on an entry you'd want to change?
- I kept **your note visually separate** from the page's own description (different colour, its own "Your note" label), so your words never get confused with the site's. Does that separation feel right?
- If you ever **clear the title** completely, I fall back to the site's name so an entry is never left nameless. Reasonable?

Once you're happy with editing, the last essential is **search** — and I'll make it reach across titles, descriptions, tags, *and* your notes.
